name: Alemtuzumab
route_note: MS: IV infusion on 5 consecutive days, then 3 days 12 months later; CLL regimens (Campath) by IV infusion three times weekly
originator: University of Cambridge (Herman Waldmann and colleagues)

discovery.by: Herman Waldmann and colleagues (University of Cambridge)
discovery.note: Rat antibody Campath-1 was humanised in 1988 by Lutz Riechmann, Greg Winter and colleagues, one of the first humanised antibodies.

tagline: Anti-CD52 antibody that resets the immune system in highly active MS
summary: Alemtuzumab is a humanised monoclonal antibody against CD52 that causes profound, long-lasting depletion of T and B lymphocytes. First approved for chronic lymphocytic leukaemia, it was relaunched at a lower dose as Lemtrada for highly active relapsing multiple sclerosis, given as two short annual courses.
mechanism: Alemtuzumab binds CD52, a glycoprotein abundant on T and B lymphocytes, NK cells, monocytes and some dendritic cells, and destroys them by antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement-mediated lysis.

Lymphocytes then repopulate over months to years with an altered repertoire — B cells recovering faster than T cells — which is thought to produce durable suppression of MS activity. The same immune reconstitution underlies frequent secondary autoimmunity.
uses: B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (Campath, where available)

history.title: Campath-1 antibody
history.detail: Waldmann's group in the Cambridge University Department of Pathology raises the rat Campath-1 antibody.

history.title: Humanisation
history.detail: Riechmann, Winter and colleagues report humanised Campath-1H in Nature.

history.title: CLL approval
history.detail: FDA approves Campath for B-cell CLL; EU approval as MabCampath follows.

history.title: Withdrawn from CLL market
history.detail: Commercial Campath is withdrawn in the US and EU ahead of relaunch for MS; access continues via a distribution programme.

history.title: Lemtrada in the EU
history.detail: Approved in the EU for relapsing-remitting MS.

history.title: Lemtrada in the US
history.detail: FDA approves Lemtrada in November after initial rejection, with a REMS programme.

history.title: EMA safety review
history.detail: EMA restricts use after reports of stroke, autoimmune hepatitis and haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

common: Upper respiratory and urinary tract infections
safety.boxed_warning: Serious, sometimes fatal autoimmune conditions (immune thrombocytopenia, anti-GBM disease); serious infusion reactions; stroke; and malignancies. Available only through a restricted programme.

facts: Campath-1H was among the first humanised monoclonal antibodies, pioneering the approach used for many later drugs.
Monthly blood and urine monitoring continues for 48 months after the last MS course to detect autoimmunity.
